subtitle: Inverted Flanger
tagline: Phase-inverted modulated delay voices carve hollow, moving notches into the sound, from slow empty-space sweeps to hard metallic motion.

body.lead: A classic flanger mixes a slowly moving delayed copy with the original. TB Inverted Flanger flips the copies upside down before mixing, so instead of a bright whoosh you get hollow cancellation: deep notches that sweep through the sound.

body.p: Three short delay voices, each with its own depth and phase, move together under one LFO. The result ranges from subtle empty-space motion to dramatic sci-fi sweeps on guitars, synths, vocals, and drum loops.

ul: Three phase-inverted delay voices with different base delays, depths, and phases
DEPTH sweeps the delay between roughly 0.1 and 8.4 ms
FEEDBACK adds resonance, limited internally to keep it under control
COLOR sets how deep the inverted notches cut, without changing the dry signal
MIX blends the inverted comb signal with the dry sound
No added latency; mono input is processed as stereo

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Inverted Flanger 2.0.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.0.2 and may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Inverted Flanger on a track. The defaults are `MIX` 52%, `DEPTH` 72%, `RATE` 0.34 Hz, `FEEDBACK` 32%, `COLOR` 68%.
Play the material and set the speed of the sweep with `RATE`.
Set how far the notches travel with `DEPTH`.
Raise `FEEDBACK` for a more resonant, jet-like sweep.
Raise `COLOR` for deeper, more hollow notches.

rows: Previous and next factory preset, the PRESET list (CUSTOM after an edit, LOAD USER PRESET... for your files), Save, Undo, and Redo.
Shows the shape of the inverted modulation. RUNNING appears while the modulation runs.
Range and speed of the sweep.
Balance between the dry sound and the inverted comb signal.
How far the delay is modulated, roughly 0.1 to 8.4 ms. More depth moves the notches across a wider frequency range.
Speed of the LFO that moves all three delay voices together. Low values give slow sweeps; high values give fast, warbling motion.
Feeds the output back into the delays for resonance and a stronger jet effect. The engine scales it by 0.9 so it cannot run away.
Level of the phase-inverted copies, from 0.4 to 1.0 of full gain. Higher values cut deeper notches. The dry signal is not affected.
Blend between the dry sound and the inverted comb signal.

body.p: Each of the three voices starts from a different short base delay (0.24, 0.42, and 0.64 ms) and moves with its own depth and phase. Their outputs are damped above about 6.8 kHz and summed upside down, so wherever a voice lines up with the dry signal, that frequency cancels. As the delays move, the cancellation notches sweep through the spectrum.

note.text: TB Inverted Flanger has no output knob and adds no latency. Because it works by cancellation, it can make a sound quieter; match levels before comparing with bypass.

body.p: Step through the factory presets with the arrows beside the preset name, or open the PRESET list. LOAD USER PRESET... opens a .tbifpreset file, and Save stores the current settings as one. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a preset. The second pair of arrows undoes and redoes changes.
Factory presets: **Empty Orbit**, **Null Corridor**, **Neon Comb**, **Signal Rift**, **Slow Eclipse**, and **10Hz Scanner**.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Hollow guitar sweep
recipes.use: Slow, deep motion on sustained guitar or pads.
steps: Raise COLOR until the hollow character is clear.

steps: Check that the transients still cut through; lower FEEDBACK if they smear.

rows: The sound got thin or quiet.
That is the cancellation at work. Lower COLOR or MIX, then match levels in your mixer.
Use lower DEPTH on bass-heavy sources and raise RATE slowly.
Raise MIX and COLOR, or raise DEPTH.
With high FEEDBACK and COLOR, check the result in mono and on the transients.
The interface was rebuilt as a warm hardware-style rack with a dedicated output waveform display, and DEPTH, RATE, FEEDBACK, COLOR, and MIX were reorganized into a clearer vertical flow.
